+## #2859 - Example case 2d/contour-tabs: one plate, one 2D Contour
+
+**What was decided.** The case `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs` is a
+90 x 50 x 6 mm plate with four 10 mm corner chamfers, in a 120 x 80 x 6 mm
+sheet. One 2D Contour cuts the outside with a 6 mm flat end mill. The lead-in
+is a 3 mm arc. The lead-out is a 4 mm line. There are four tabs, 8 mm wide
+and 2 mm high. The stepdown is 2 mm, so the levels are Z4, Z2 and Z0.
+
+**Why.**
+
+- One operation keeps the program short (104 lines). A reader sees each lead
+  move and each tab lift without a search.
+- The outline has only straight edges. Each `G03` block is then a lead-in,
+  and each `G02` block is a corner roll. The pinning test counts them.
+- An arc lead-in and a linear lead-out are two different shapes. The program
+  shows that the two parameters are independent.
+- The sheet is as thick as the plate. The contour goes to the sheet bottom,
+  and the tabs are the only material that holds the plate. This is the usual
+  cut-out job.
+- The stepdown equals the tab height. The tab top (Z2) is a level of the
+  stepdown ladder, and no extra level is added (#2579).
+- The model is a prism that the generator script writes. No outside geometry
+  is used (Clean-Room Protocol).
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- A plate with holes and a Drill operation. The seed case `2d/first-part`
+  shows Drill. A second operation hides the lead moves and the tab lifts.
+- A rectangle. The chamfers give corners that are not 90 degrees and make
+  the geometry original for this case.
+- A stock top above the plate top with a Face operation. It adds levels and
+  an operation that this case does not show.
+- A lead-in written as `lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } }`. `add_operation`
+  refuses it: the patch merges with the seeded linear lead, and the result
+  has two shapes. The script writes `linear: null` with the arc. The refusal
+  message does not name the cause; #2876 is the bug for it.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small. Change `build.camscript`, run
+`cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/contour-tabs`, and update the counts in the
+test `contour_tabs_case_posts_the_lead_moves_and_the_tab_lifts`.
+
+**Pinned by.** `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`:
+`contour_tabs_case_posts_the_lead_moves_and_the_tab_lifts`, and the two
+catalog tests that read each case.
+
+**Review fix (PR #2877).** Keep the imported mesh embedded, and remove its
+source link in both the committed project and `build.camscript`. The UI
+checks a relative source path from the process directory. The example must
+open when that directory differs from the case directory. The seed project
+also embeds its mesh without a source link. An absolute path would tie the
+example to one checkout. A product path-resolution change is outside this
+example fix. The two app catalog tests pin the embedded mesh and the absent
+link in the committed and rebuilt projects. The existing UI catalog test
+checks that the committed project opens.

+# Contour with Tabs (2D Contour, lead-in, lead-out, tabs)
+
+A 90 x 50 x 6 mm clean-room plate with four 10 mm corner chamfers. One 2D Contour cuts it out of a 120 x 80 x 6 mm sheet. Four tabs hold the plate in the sheet.
+
+## What it shows
+
+1. **2D Contour (`2D Contour1`, `EM-0600-4FL`):** Cuts the outside of the plate, climb, in three levels: `Z4`, `Z2` and `Z0` (the sheet bottom). The stepdown is 2 mm.
+2. **Lead-in:** A 3 mm arc (`lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } }`). Each cut run starts with one `G03` block that ends tangent to the outline.
+3. **Lead-out:** A 4 mm line (`links.approach.lead_out`). Each cut run ends with one `G01` block before the tool lifts.
+4. **Tabs:** Four tabs, 8 mm wide and 2 mm high. The levels `Z4` and `Z2` cut the whole ring. `Z2` is the tab top. The level `Z0` is four runs, and the tool lifts over each tab.
+
+## What to look at
+
+- In `contour-tabs.nc`, the levels `Z4` and `Z2` each have one `G03` lead-in and one lift.
+- The level `Z0` has four `G03` lead-ins and four lifts. The first three lifts are `G01` moves to the retract height `Z11`. The last lift is the `G00` move to the clearance height `Z21`.
+- The gap between two `Z0` runs is larger than the tab width plus the tool diameter (14 mm). The tab fit moves the runs apart until the two lead moves leave the full 8 mm of the tab.
+- The outline corners are `G02` arcs of 3 mm radius: the tool centre rolls around each sharp corner of the plate.
+- `build.camscript` sets `lead` with `linear: null`. `add_operation` applies `params` as a merge patch on the seeded linear lead, and a lead holds one shape only (#2876).
+- The program cuts to `Z0`, the bottom of the sheet. On a machine, the sheet is on a spoilboard.
+
+## Files
+
+- `model/gen_contour_tabs_obj.py` — generator for the plate: a prism over one octagon, with a watertight check.
+- `model/contour-tabs.obj` — generated mesh imported by `build.camscript`.
+- `build.camscript` — headless script building `contour-tabs.camproj` and posting `contour-tabs.nc` through CamCraft's undoable commands.
+- `contour-tabs.camproj` — committed project with the generated toolpath.
+- `contour-tabs.nc` — committed Fanuc NC program verified byte-for-byte in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.
+
+## Rebuild and verify
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/contour-tabs
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+```

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regenerate contour-tabs.obj, the model of the catalog case 2d/contour-tabs.
+
+The part is a clean-room Camcraft fixture: a 90 x 50 x 6 mm plate with four
+10 mm corner chamfers, centred on the XY origin, z from 0 to 6. A 2D Contour
+cuts it out of a 120 x 80 x 6 mm sheet and leaves four tabs.
+
+Method: the solid is a prism over one convex octagon. The top and the bottom
+are triangle fans from the first corner, and each side is one quad. All faces
+share the same sixteen corners, so the mesh has no T-junctions. The script
+checks that the mesh is watertight and consistently oriented before it
+writes the file.
+
+Usage: python gen_contour_tabs_obj.py [output.obj]
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+HALF_X = 45.0
+HALF_Y = 25.0
+CHAMFER = 10.0
+Z_BOTTOM = 0.0
+Z_TOP = 6.0
+
+# Counter-clockwise seen from +Z.
+OUTLINE = [
+    (HALF_X - CHAMFER, -HALF_Y),
+    (HALF_X, -HALF_Y + CHAMFER),
+    (HALF_X, HALF_Y - CHAMFER),
+    (HALF_X - CHAMFER, HALF_Y),
+    (-HALF_X + CHAMFER, HALF_Y),
+    (-HALF_X, HALF_Y - CHAMFER),
+    (-HALF_X, -HALF_Y + CHAMFER),
+    (-HALF_X + CHAMFER, -HALF_Y),
+]
+
+
+def build():
+    n = len(OUTLINE)
+    bottom = [(x, y, Z_BOTTOM) for x, y in OUTLINE]
+    top = [(x, y, Z_TOP) for x, y in OUTLINE]
+    faces = []
+    for i in range(1, n - 1):
+        faces.append([top[0], top[i], top[i + 1]])            # normal +Z
+        faces.append([bottom[0], bottom[i + 1], bottom[i]])   # normal -Z
+    for i in range(n):
+        j = (i + 1) % n
+        faces.append([bottom[i], bottom[j], top[j], top[i]])  # normal outward
+    return faces
+
+
+def check(faces):
+    """Watertight and consistently oriented: every directed edge appears
+    exactly once and its reverse appears exactly once."""
+    seen = set()
+    for face in faces:
+        for p, q in zip(face, face[1:] + face[:1]):
+            if p == q:
+                raise SystemExit("degenerate face: %r" % (face,))
+            if (p, q) in seen:
+                raise SystemExit("directed edge reused: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+            seen.add((p, q))
+    for (p, q) in seen:
+        if (q, p) not in seen:
+            raise SystemExit("open edge: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+
+
+def main():
+    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "contour-tabs.obj"
+    faces = build()
+    check(faces)
+
+    vid = {}
+    vlines = []
+    for face in faces:
+        for p in face:
+            if p not in vid:
+                vid[p] = len(vlines) + 1
+                vlines.append("v %g %g %g" % p)
+    flines = ["f " + " ".join(str(vid[p]) for p in face) for face in faces]
+
+    with open(out, "w") as fh:
+        fh.write(HEADER)
+        fh.write("\n" + "\n".join(vlines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(flines) + "\n")
+    print("wrote %s: %d vertices, %d faces" % (out, len(vlines), len(flines)))
+
+
+HEADER = """\
+# Camcraft example catalog, case 2d/contour-tabs: a 90 x 50 x 6 mm plate
+# with four 10 mm corner chamfers, centred on the XY origin, z 0 to 6.
+# Authored for this repository (clean-room fixture); generated by
+# gen_contour_tabs_obj.py as a watertight mesh."""
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
